Front: Four domains of palliative care assessment?
Back: Physical, psychological, social, existential/spiritual

Front: P-SPIKES steps for breaking bad news?
Back: Preparation, Setting, Perception, Invitation, Knowledge, Empathy, Summary and planning

Front: Medicare hospice eligibility?
Back: Two physicians certify prognosis of 6 months or less if the disease runs its usual course

Front: Does the Medicare hospice benefit cover curative therapy for the terminal illness?
Back: No; other comorbid conditions are still treated, and enrollment can be revoked

Front: The 'surprise question' for prognosis?
Back: 'Would I be surprised if this patient died in the next 12 months?'

Front: Opioid regimen for continuous cancer pain?
Back: Around-the-clock dosing plus rescue doses (~20% of baseline) for breakthrough pain

Front: Opioid-naive patient with severe cancer pain: short- or long-acting first?
Back: Short-acting to establish the 24-48 h need, then convert to extended-release

Front: How to escalate opioids if pain persists after 24 h?
Back: Add the total rescue doses used to the daily dose, or increase 50% (moderate) / 100% (severe)

Front: Starting dose when switching to a different opioid?
Back: 50-75% of the published equianalgesic dose (incomplete cross-tolerance)

Front: Do opioids have a ceiling dose?
Back: No; the right dose is whatever relieves the pain

Front: First-line adjuvant for neuropathic cancer pain?
Back: Gabapentin

Front: Treatment for bone pain from a single metastasis?
Back: Radiation therapy (radiopharmaceuticals like strontium-89 for multiple metastases)

Front: Max acetaminophen dose in cirrhosis (per Harrison)?
Back: 2 g/day

Front: Opioid-induced constipation prophylaxis?
Back: Laxative plus stool softener, e.g., senna plus docusate, started with the opioid

Front: Refractory opioid-induced constipation drug and mechanism?
Back: Methylnaltrexone; peripheral opioid antagonist that preserves central analgesia

Front: First-line drug for dyspnea at the end of life?
Back: Low-dose opioid (oxygen is no better than air)

Front: When are benzodiazepines used for end-of-life dyspnea?
Back: Only when anxiety is present; never first-line

Front: Antiemetic for anticipatory nausea?
Back: Benzodiazepine (lorazepam)

Front: Antiemetic for vestibular nausea?
Back: Meclizine or scopolamine

Front: Depression with a prognosis of weeks: drug class?
Back: Psychostimulant (methylphenidate), works in days

Front: SSRI starting dose in seriously ill patients?
Back: Half the usual starting dose (e.g., fluoxetine 10 mg)

Front: First-line drug for terminal delirium?
Back: Haloperidol (PO/SC/IV; avoid IM)

Front: Management of the 'death rattle'?
Back: Scopolamine, repositioning, reassurance; do not suction

Front: Should a dying patient who stops eating get IV fluids or tube feeds?
Back: No; they don't relieve symptoms or prolong life, and fluids can worsen dyspnea and edema

Front: Steps before terminal ventilator withdrawal?
Back: Stop neuromuscular blockers; give benzodiazepine bolus plus morphine bolus and infusion

Front: Main drivers of requests for physician-assisted suicide?
Back: Depression, hopelessness, loss of autonomy and dignity (not usually pain)

Front: Initial response to a request for physician-assisted suicide?
Back: Open-ended exploration of the reasons, e.g., 'What makes you want to consider this option?'

Front: Who should the family call when a hospice patient dies at home?
Back: Hospice or the on-call clinician, not 911
